full_judgment:
Hasan Foez Siddique J. These two Criminal Petitions have been filed by the Anti-Corruption Commission and the State against the same judgment and order dated 09.07.2014 kissed by the High Court Division in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 17818 of 2014 enlarging the respondent Dr. Khondaker Mosharraf Hossain on bail till submission of the police report. 

 2. Mr. A.M. Mahbubuddin, learned Counsel appearing for the respondent in both the petitions, submits that in the instant case police report has already been submitted consequently both the petitions have become infructuous. 

 "According to the law enunciated in the case of Anti-Corruption Commission Vs. Dr. Mohiuddin Khan Alamgir and others 62 DLR (AD) 290, no charge sheet yet been submitted against the accused petitioner, no case is legally deemed to have been instituted against him. But, unless a case is legally deemed to have been instituted against any person, no Court can either take cognizance of the offence or issue any process against such a person and accordingly, if any person is apprehended or arrested and brought before any Court should at least set him at large." 

 5. While making aforesaid observations the High Court Division relied on its earlier unreported decision in the case of Abdullah Al Mamun and another Vs. the State (Number of the said case has not been mentioned in the impugned judgment). The following paragraphs of the said judgment are relevant her to quote: 

 (7) Since the allegations arc to be investigated in to exclusively by the Commission, the police, on their own accord, cannot arrest any accused-per-son before or after submission of the Investigation Report in any such case. 

 (8) In view of the above, no accused-person legally requires any bail during investigation in any such case. 

 (8) there is no legal scope or necessity for any anticipatory bail in any case no the allegations of the offences under the ACC Act, 2004 and the offences included or deemed to have been, included in the schedule of the Act." 

 6. The observations of the High Court Division in this case and the above quoted paragraphs of Abdullah Al Mamun's case are not based on correct proposition of law. 

 7. The "offence" committed within the mischief of the Money Laundering Protirodh Ain is cognizable. Non-compoundable and non-bailable, "Offence" means any act or omission made punishable by any law for the time being in force. Cognizable offence means an offence for which a police officer may, in accordance with the second schedule of the Code of Criminal Procedure or under any other law for the time being in force, arrest the person (s) related to the offence without warrant. The words "under any law for the time being in force" are wide enough to include an express or implied provision of any law or enactment. If any "offence" is committed within the mischief of Money Laundering Protirodh Ain, the police may arrest the person related with such offence without warrant. 

 8. Neither in the Code of Criminal Procedure nor in the Durniti Daman Commission Ain nor in the judgment delivered by this Division in the case of Durnity Daman Commission Vs. Dr. Mohiuddin Khan Alamger reported in 62 DLR (AD) 290 it has been said that investigating agencies are not empowered to arrest any person in connection with an cognizable offence before institution of a case. Since the allegation against the petitioner is that he has committed a cognizible offence there is no legal impediment to arrest him.
